images.scene: A confident 1950s star salesman lounging at his steel tanker desk: pinstripe suit, both feet up on the desktop, cigarette in one hand, a large metal sales trophy standing beside a black rotary phone, grinning like he owns the place. Seen frontally from mid distance, the man and his desk are LARGE in the frame, filling the bottom half and bleeding off the bottom edge. The office behind him dissolves into bright pale haze.

A 1950s open-plan sales office seen from the side: one salesman strolling casually across the floor with his suit jacket slung over his shoulder, unhurried, while the other salesmen sit hunched over black rotary phones at steel desks, heads down. A large round wall clock hangs in the background haze. All figures sit low in the frame, desks bleeding off the bottom edge.

Waist-up close of a 1950s business owner standing in his sales office, arms crossed tight over his chest, jaw clenched, eyes deliberately averted downward and to the side, refusing to speak, uncomfortable silence on his face. His figure LARGE in the frame filling the bottom half, bleeding off the bottom edge; behind him the office dissolves into bright pale haze.

A large dark blackboard leaning against an office wall with a hand-drawn chalk bar chart: one single tall bar towering far above a row of small stubby bars, plain chalk strokes only, no letters and no numerals anywhere. A wooden chalk ledge with dust below. The blackboard sits low in the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge, the pale plaster wall above it washed in bright haze.

In a 1950s sales office, ALL figures and furniture strictly confined to the BOTTOM HALF of the frame, the entire upper half completely empty pale haze with nothing in it. In the bottom half: a tight closed circle of four salesmen in suits laughing together with their backs turned outward, huddled around a desk on one side; on the other side, separated by a stretch of empty floor, a very young new salesman stands alone holding his briefcase, shut out of the circle, his head well below the vertical middle of the frame.

Seen from behind at close range: the backs of four salesmen in dark suits standing shoulder to shoulder, forming a closed human wall that blocks the way, no faces visible, cigarette smoke rising between them. The wall of backs fills the bottom half of the frame, bleeding off the bottom and side edges; above their shoulders the office dissolves into bright pale empty haze.

A chest X-ray film held by two metal clips on a glowing wall-mounted lightbox in a mid-century doctor's office, seen frontally at close range. The lightbox sits low in the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge, and its glow washes the wall above into bright pale haze. No people, no text on the film.

A vast 1950s sales floor with rows of desks shrouded in dusty white sheets like furniture in an abandoned house; only one desk in the far back is uncovered and occupied, a small desk lamp glowing over a lone working man. Wide shot, the sheeted desks low in the frame and bleeding off the bottom edge, the ceiling space above dissolved in bright pale haze.

A large dark blackboard leaning against an office wall with a single hand-drawn chalk line chart that swings violently up and down in wild jagged zigzags, like a fever chart out of control, plain chalk strokes only, absolutely no letters and no numerals anywhere. A wooden chalk ledge below. The blackboard sits low in the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge, the pale plaster wall above washed in bright haze.

Extreme macro still life: the swung-open cylinder of a vintage revolver lying flat on a dark wooden meeting table, a single brass cartridge seated in one chamber of the empty cylinder, shallow depth of field, quiet and ominous. The revolver sits low in the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge. The table surface behind it falls out of focus and fades upward into bright pale haze. No people, no hands.

A 1950s business owner alone in his office late at night, sitting at his desk lit only by a small banker's desk lamp, one hand on his chin, staring down at the black rotary telephone in front of him. The man and desk sit low in the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge; the lamp glow and smoke-like haze wash the entire upper half of the frame bright and pale.

In the near foreground a vacated steel desk with all its drawers pulled open and empty, papers gone; in the background, framed by strict one-point perspective, a man in a suit seen from behind walks out through the office door carrying a cardboard box under his arm. The door is the vanishing point, dissolving into pale light. Desk and figure low in the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge.

Close-up over a wooden desk: one man's hand pushing a thick stuffed paper envelope across the surface toward another open hand reaching to receive it, caught mid-motion. Cuffs of two different suits visible at the frame edges. Hands and envelope sit low in the frame, the desk bleeding off the bottom edge, the space above the hands bright, pale and empty.

A 1950s sales office wall: a freshly hung wooden framed notice board holding a plain ruled sheet with faint blank chalk lines only, no letters, hanging LOW on the wall with its bottom edge almost touching the steel desks below it; the entire upper 60 percent of the frame is bare empty pale plaster wall with nothing on it. Below the board, steel desks in perfect alignment bleeding off the bottom edge; in the front row, two chairs stand empty, pushed away from their desks at an angle. Sense of new order.

A long row of identical steel tanker desks, each with an identical black rotary phone in the identical position, receding in strict one-point perspective toward a pale vanishing point, perfectly symmetric, machine-like order, no people. The desks fill the bottom half, bleeding off the bottom edge, upper half of the frame bright, pale and empty.

A lively 1950s sales floor seen from a high wide angle: half a dozen young salesmen in rolled-up shirtsleeves talking energetically into rotary phones at their desks, one standing with the receiver to his ear; on the far wall a blackboard with a single hand-drawn chalk line climbing steadily upward, no letters and no numerals. Figures and desks low in the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge, upper half bright hazy pale.

Seen from behind at waist height in the near foreground, a business owner standing calm and still with his arms crossed, soft backlight rimming his shoulders, watching over his full sales floor working in the hazy distance: rows of desks, men on phones, quiet motion. His dark silhouette occupies the lower third and bleeds off the bottom edge; the office beyond dissolves into bright pale haze filling the upper half.

A dusty old metal sales trophy standing forgotten on a high wooden shelf, in sharp focus, cobwebs at its base; beyond and below it, thrown far out of focus, the sales office floor keeps working without it, blurred figures at desks. The trophy and shelf sit low in the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge, the wall above washed in bright pale haze.
